Although the origin has not been definitely identified, S5’s spectra appear to be contaminated so its DR2 radial velocity has been excluded from EDR3.

notes: Gaia DR2 5932173855446728064 (S1) is treated as follow_up because T:p3-b2 calls it the premier hypervelocity star candidate in DR2 and states its DR2 radial velocity alone was sufficient to class it as a hypervelocity star; the paper later rejects that DR2 velocity. Gaia DR2 5716044263405220096, Gaia DR2 5850309098637075328, and Gaia DR2 5966712023814100736 (S5) are follow_up because T:p17-b12 explicitly lists them as Li et al. (2020)'s three late-type hypervelocity star candidates. For S5, the general statement at T:p12-b1 that all six Table 2 stars had rv_nb_transits < 5 and were not used in high-velocity studies conflicts with that explicit Li et al. identification; I followed the explicit candidate identification. Table A.1 at T:p23-b0 supports identical EDR3 source IDs for S1 and S5; 'EDR3: No' in Table B.1 means the DR2 radial velocity was not propagated, not that the source has no EDR3 ID. Gaia DR2 1995066395528322560 is not included: T:p17-b13 says it is in the B19 list and that Li et al. obtained a radial velocity, but does not explicitly identify it as a hypervelocity/unbound candidate. Stars tabulated in Tables B.1 and B.2 are described only as high-velocity stars at T:p28-b3, not as established Galactic unbound candidates, so they were not included merely for having |RV| > 500 km/s.

Gaia DR2 5932173855446728064: T:p3-b2 quotes S1's DR2 radial velocity as −614.3 ± 2.4 km/s, whereas T:p3-b7 and Table B.1 at T:p29-b0 give −614.3 ± 2.5 km/s; I treat the ±2.4 as a typo and retain ±2.5. T:p4-b16 states that the CU6-DR3 operational run did not output a radial velocity for S1.

Gaia DR2 5716044263405220096: The paper (Sect. 4.2.4, T:p17-b12) lists three Li et al. (2020) DR2 source IDs (5716044263405220096, 5850309098637075328, 5966712023814100736) and states that the first two are in EDR3 with DR2 radial velocities −453.5 ± 2.4 and −486.9 ± 5.0 km/s. Values are assigned in the listed order, so 5716044263405220096 receives −453.5 ± 2.4 km/s. No other quantities (position, parallax, distance, proper motion, etc.) are reported for this star.

Gaia DR2 5850309098637075328: The target star 5850309098637075328 is the second of the three Li et al. (2020) candidates listed in Sect. 4.2.4; the quoted DR2 radial velocities are given in the same order as the source IDs (5716044263405220096: -453.5 ± 2.4 km/s; 5850309098637075328: -486.9 ± 5.0 km/s; 5966712023814100736: -967.7 ± 5.8 km/s). The star is stated to be in EDR3, meaning its DR2 radial velocity was retained. No astrometric quantities, distance, parallax or Galactic kinematics are reported for this star in the supplied material; it does not appear in Tables B.1/B.2 because |RV| < 500 km/s.

Gaia DR2 5966712023814100736: The target is S5 = Gaia DR2/EDR3 5966712023814100736. Table B.1 lists its DR2 RV as -967.7 ± 5.8 km/s with EDR3 status "No"; Appendix A.3 concludes its DR2 radial velocity is excluded from EDR3 because the spectra appear contaminated. No DR3 radial velocity is reported for this source, and no astrometric, distance, parallax, or Galactic-orbit quantities are reported for it in this paper.
